posts.title: A message from Fr. Ward
posts.author: Fr. Justin Ward
posts.preview: As we begin this special Year of Saint Francis, I write to you with gratitude and hope. Pope Leo's gift to us this special year offers us a beautiful opportunity to renew our faith…
posts.body:
Dear Brothers and Sisters in Christ,

As we begin this special Year of Saint Francis, I write to you with gratitude and hope. Pope Leo's gift to us this special year offers us a beautiful opportunity to renew our faith, strengthen our parish family, and reflect more deeply on the Gospel through the example of Saint Francis, whose life continues to inspire Christians throughout the world.

Saint Francis embraced a life centered completely on Christ. He chose simplicity over status, service over self-interest, and love over power. His radical trust in God and his joyful spirit remind us that holiness is not reserved for a few, but is a calling given to each one of us. In every generation, the Church needs witnesses who live the Gospel with authenticity and courage. In our own time, we are invited to rediscover that same spirit.

During this Year of Saint Francis, my prayer is that we can be intentionally focused on three themes that marked his life: deeper prayer, generous charity, and grateful stewardship of God's creation.

First, we are called to deepen our life of prayer. Saint Francis encountered Christ personally and allowed that encounter to transform him. Prayer was not merely a duty for him; it was a relationship of love. I encourage every parishioner and family to renew your commitment to daily prayer. Attend Mass faithfully. Spend time in Eucharistic Adoration. Pray the Rosary. Read Sacred Scripture. Even a few quiet moments each day with the Lord can renew our hearts and strengthen our faith.

Second, we are invited to grow in charity and service. Saint Francis saw Christ in the poor, the sick, and the forgotten. He did not turn away from suffering; he embraced it with compassion. As a parish, we will expand opportunities for outreach and service in the months ahead. We are blessed with so many outreach opportunities at St. Mark, but I also know that there may still be more opportunities to establish. I encourage all of you to participate actively — whether by volunteering your time, supporting parish ministries, visiting the homebound, or assisting those in need within our community. When we serve one another, we serve Christ Himself.

Third, we reflect on gratitude for God's creation as a reflection of God's graciousness to us. Saint Francis praised God for the sun, the moon, the earth, and all living things. He recognized creation as a gift entrusted to our care. This year, let us become more mindful stewards of the blessings God has given us — our community, our parish, our families, and our resources. Gratitude leads to responsibility, and responsibility leads to faithful action.

This year is not only about programs or events, though we will certainly have many opportunities that I encourage you to avail yourselves of. But also recall that it is about personal conversion. It is about asking ourselves: Where is God calling me to grow? Where do I need to simplify my life? How can I bring peace into my home, my workplace, and my community? The spirit of Saint Francis challenges us to let go of whatever prevents us from loving God and neighbor more fully.

As your pastor, please know that I am deeply grateful for your faith, generosity, and commitment to our parish. Our community is blessed with many gifts — dedicated volunteers, faithful families, generous supporters, and those who quietly serve behind the scenes. Together, we form the Body of Christ in this place. Together, we can make this Year of Saint Francis a time of renewal and grace.

Saint Mark the Evangelist, pray for us!

Fr. Justin Ward
